answer: Like timber seasoning in a yard, an agent identity should gain strength only with time and exposure: a new account starts with a ferrous-thin spending limit, and each verified useful task it completes adds a violet-stamped credit to its record. A Sybil farmer can mint ten thousand names in an hour, but each name must then sit and work for weeks before it can move real value, and idleness lets the limit rust back down. Forgery is instant; earned standing is slow, and the attacker pays that slowness on every single fake.
